reviewer.note: docs/reviews/2026-11-04-woodland-water.md, round 6 (5725cf90). K5-1 is fixed: measured independently on the picture and on every frame of the loop (sheet body rows 20 to foot-4, interior columns), lightness changes 4.7 to 10.9 x as often across as down and the median vertical run of one colour is 6 to 15 texels (the one-tier pieces 6 to 11; the lowest, 6.0, in waterfall_2 frame 2 and the waterfall_3 and _4 pictures); the woodland sheet measures 9.5 and 14. It reads as falling water at 1x beside Bramble and in the woodland_kit and kitlab_tiers bakes (Godot under Xvfb). It fails on K6-1: the value structure is not its sibling's. Frame 0 overlaid, the body's mean lightness is 134 to 142 L against the woodland sheet's 171, its east half 98 to 110 against 153; texels under 90 L are 15 to 21 % of the body (east 40 %: 32 to 47 %) against 8 % (19 %); texels over 200 L in the middle third 20 to 26 % against 41 %, in the east third none against 26 %. So the sheet is a dark blue curtain with a lit west strip, not the woodland's lit mass falling to a narrow dark east edge (5.3b: "a lit west part and a darker east edge"; one design per object), and the dark east part pools into flat navy slabs (waterfall_4_tall frame 0: one 826-texel (30,66,122) area over x 91-119, rows 20-103). Fix: in structures.fall_sheet, the body tone water 4 to s 0.45 and water 3 to s 0.88, the dark tones only in the last 2 to 4 texels (s 0.88 on), the alternate-lane deepening only east of s 0.5 and never below water 2, lit runs snow 5 to s 0.45, snow 4 to s 0.7, water 5 to s 0.88; test mean L at least 160, east half at least 140, under-90 share at most 0.10, middle-third lit share at least 0.35, beside fall_grain. Polish P6-1: the edges keep x 24 and x 24+w except two one-texel indents of 6 to 7 rows and the last-third swell; the woodland edge treatment (a pale film west, a soft navy edge east) and a shorter wander period would take the ruler off. Polish carried from round 5: the tongue in rows 12-14 still splits into two tones at a hard vertical seam.
